brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Quorvo, the meeting assistant in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: calm, competent and human; for remote teams who are tired of meetings. No sparkles, stars, brains, robots, chat bubbles, waveforms or gradient blobs. Web app, a desktop app icon (macOS, Windows) and social.

claim.notes: Only the wordmark-led underline concept passed the critic's gate (narrowly, blind 6/6/7) out of five directions over two rounds; it was finalized with an accepted insufficient-evidence originality risk, exported for web, macOS, Windows and social, with a dry-run Next.js install plan and gallery built.

concepts.title: Cairn
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a piggy bank or toilet seen from the side, a coin slot / the digit 0 on a shelf; s7 a ghost or round face with an exclamation mark; s8 an egg or pawn above a progress bar with a dot ('0.' / loading); s9 the letter S beside an orange tombstone or door. None reads as a trail blaze: the blaze needs a tree trunk or rock context to be a blaze, and stripped down it becomes a slot or a bar. s9's orange rounded slab is a gravestone, an unfortunate reading for a meeting tool; s6/s7 blob boulders are close to the gradient-blob form the owner banned, and lumpy organics at this size feel unfinished rather than calm. Second round failed to land the waymark; retire the direction.

concepts.title: Door ajar
readsAs: a Greek capital Gamma or a squared-off r beside a slanted gold block (r + ramp, 'rA')
a doorstop or ramp wedge standing next to a bracket
a doorway with light falling through (only third, and only on reflection) -- unfortunate: an exit/leave sign, a cheese wedge
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 the letter N (struck, different letter); s2 an open door in perspective — closest to the idea but reads as the logout/exit UI icon (struck); s3 a desk lamp or a spotlight cone with an L, the door is lost; s4 a slim dark jamb with a wedge of warm light falling from a crack — first reading door-crack light, second a sail; s5 letters (lambda/JL) and a floor-plan symbol, weak at 16 px (85%) and architectural, not human. Keep s4: the light is the mark, amber on slate breaks the category's blue/purple tiles, calm and human. Fix: (1) kill the sail reading — the wedge must start AT the jamb's top along its full height edge, apex touching the crack, not a free-standing triangle; consider a short lintel/head stub so it's a doorway, not a mast; (2) make the jamb-to-wedge gap the deliberate crack, consistent width; (3) give the wedge's floor edge a slight soft taper rather than a hard sharp corner so it reads as light, not a blade/flag; (4) test against flashlight-beam and Fireflies/tl;dv at 16 px. Risk: door+light-wedge is a known stock motif; ownability comes only from the exact jamb/crack proportion.

concepts.title: Fold
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 tally marks or equalizer bars next to a card (finance/tally cliché, 'IIII'); s2 a paperclip or magnet hook / a 'J' — no fold reads; s3 a pause glyph beside a card, or a deck of cards; s4 a loudspeaker/volume UI icon (square + flared trapezoid). No sketch reads as folding or as 'the page that matters'; every one lands on a UI icon or the product's own object (page/card). Struck all. The fold idea needs a visible crease to read at all, and a crease on a rectangle is a folded-page cliché; do not develop this direction further.

concepts.title: Loose end
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s5 the chain-link (hyperlink) UI icon, broken; s6 a pretzel / link icon with a dragged tail; s7 the link icon in a stock green squircle (stock 0.86); s8 link icon / scribbled 'cl'. At 16 px all four collapse to a squiggle. The overhand knot drawn as two interlocking stroked arcs is indistinguishable from the hyperlink glyph, a UI icon, which is struck; the dashed broken ends add a 'broken link' reading, the opposite of the idea. Second round with the same motif: the knot does not read as a knot at icon size. Retire the direction; a rework of this drawing will not clear blind distinctiveness.

concepts.title: Underline
readsAs: a warm serif lowercase word whose q-descender swashes into an underline, like a hand-underlined note
the symbol alone as 'q_' / 'qL', a lowercase q with a typing-cursor underscore
a classic display-serif swash tail (the generic 'signature underline' trope). Unfortunate: the standalone q_ reads as a terminal prompt/placeholder or an unfinished letter
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a lowercase q whose tail turns into an underline (close to the idea; secondary reading q joined to an L); s2 a q on a ski / a tail ending in a tick (checkmark cliché risk); s3 'q.' a letter plus full stop, a common device, the dot drops out at 16 px; s4 a q on a pedestal / stamp handle. Pick s1: the only one where the tail itself becomes the rule, which is exactly what carries into the wordmark. Risks: as an icon it is still an initial-letter glyph in a category full of them, so the drawing must be ownable (do not ship stock Fraunces; draw the bend as one deliberate soft turn with a slight stroke swell, and make the rule long enough that it reads as underline, not as a joined L). In the wordmark, test early that the rule under 'uorvo' does not read as a hyperlink underline or a text-field cursor; stop the rule short of the final o or vary its weight so it reads as a pen stroke. Check Qorvo neighbour.
